home.edition: FROM FIRST SIGNAL TO FINAL SETTLEMENT

audiences.title: Capital with a structure. Not just a story.

home.encoreEyebrow: THE END OF ONE SHOW. THE START OF THE NEXT.

ecosystem.title: Every part has a role. All share the rhythm.
ecosystem.intro: CORTEX is the platform. Its components connect demand, capital, execution, and settlement in a learning loop.
ecosystem.label: PRODUCT ARCHITECTURE
ecosystem.learningBody: Every event's outcome feeds the underwriting of the next.

items.name: CT-GOT
items.headline: Read the demand. Before committing the capital.
items.body: Models sell-through probability, break-even velocity, and risk. Updates the forecast as new signals arrive.
items.handoff: Demand signals → scenarios for financing decisions.

items.name: Capital / SPV
items.headline: One event. A defined financial structure.
items.body: An event vehicle separates obligations and coordinates capital, collateral, and terms. PRONESYS / S.P.A.R.C. Notes is the first proposed product for qualified investors.
items.handoff: Risk assessment → vehicle, terms, and financing.

items.name: GatePass
items.headline: The pulse of the event, from the first ticket.
items.body: Connects tickets, access, inventory, and identity. Execution data feeds operational monitoring and updated CT-GOT forecasts.
items.handoff: Sales and access → execution data and verifiable close.

items.name: SplitNight
items.headline: Clear rules. From close to settlement.
items.body: Applies a defined waterfall: senior priority, platform fee, and residual split. The process distinguishes success, cancellation with refunds, and exceptions.
items.handoff: Attested close → obligations, payouts, and learning.

home.title: The operating system for financing live events.
home.lead: CORTEX turns an artist opportunity into an underwritable transaction: demand forecasts, an event vehicle, capital, monitoring, and settlement.
home.problemTitle: Capital goes in before revenue. Evidence arrives afterward.
home.problemBody: Promoters commit before ticket sales begin. Investors lack continuous visibility. Cross-border capital adds legal and settlement friction.
home.loop: One platform. One lifecycle per event.
home.loopHint: Scroll or select a stage to explore its role.
home.pillar1Body: CT-GOT estimates demand, break-even, and risk, then recalculates as sales arrive.
home.pillar2Body: An event vehicle coordinates terms, collateral, and local financing.
home.pillar3Body: Ticketing, sponsors, and execution feed decisions and verifiable settlement.
home.closing: Every event produces evidence for underwriting the next one.

stages.title: Underwrite
stages.body: Risk and return scenarios from CT-GOT.

problem.title: Live-event capital arrives late and with limited visibility.
problem.lead: An opportunity may be visible long before enough evidence exists to finance it quickly.

cards.title: Concentrated promoter risk
cards.body: Artist guarantees and venue holds are paid before final sales are known.

cards.title: Opaque accounting
cards.body: Fragmented box-office data delays diligence, audit, and repayment.

cards.title: Terms that constrain artists
cards.body: Some agreements claim broad rights and delay post-tour settlement.

problem.chain: Fragmented signals → manual diligence → slow capital
problem.outro: CORTEX connects demand evidence, financing, and outcomes in a loop for each event.

solution.title: One loop connects forecasting, financing, and settlement.
solution.lead: Select a stage. Every step creates data or evidence for the next one.

nodes.title: Signals
nodes.body: Tickets, venue, public interest, and sponsors feed underwriting.

nodes.title: CT-GOT forecast
nodes.body: Estimates sales, break-even, and risk before and during the transaction.

nodes.title: Event vehicle
nodes.body: Documents terms, capital allocation, and event governance.

nodes.title: GatePass
nodes.body: Records tickets, access, inventory, and identity to observe execution.

nodes.title: Attested close
nodes.body: Confirms whether the event completed, canceled, or needs review.

nodes.title: SplitNight payout
nodes.body: Applies an agreed priority waterfall and conditions.

nodes.title: Learning loop
nodes.body: Compares forecasts with outcomes to improve the next underwriting.

solution.aside: From first signal to verifiable outcome.

ctgot.title: Financing decisions grounded in demand and risk.
ctgot.lead: CT-GOT models sales velocity, artist-market fit, capacity, and break-even probability. Underwriting updates with execution data.

gates.title: Demand
gates.body: Sales curves and probability of covering costs.

ctgot.demoIntro: All four samples are synthetic. This example's PASS rule requires P(break-even) ≥ 70% and closing p50 sales ≥ break-even; it is not a real investment policy.

investors.title: S.P.A.R.C. Notes: private credit tied to each event.
investors.lead: PRONESYS proposes senior notes backed by primary ticketing flows, with event-specific terms and eligibility criteria.
investors.target3Label: target flat preferred return per tour leg, plus possible upside
investors.targetNote: Indicative targets from the PRONESYS material. Not guaranteed returns; structure and availability depend on legal and transaction review.
investors.structureBody: The event vehicle is designed to isolate obligations and proceeds. Security rights, repayment priority, and recourse depend on documents and jurisdiction.
investors.collateralBody: An overcollateralized reserve is intended to absorb drawdowns and cover shortfalls under agreed terms; losses remain possible. Custody is to be confirmed.
investors.custodyTodo: TODO: confirm collateral custody and legal treatment in each jurisdiction.
tiers: 2 · Platform fee (2–3% in the source deck)
3 · Residual split between promoter and artist
investors.calculatorIntro: Enter assumptions to see payment order. If funds run short, part of the senior obligation remains unpaid; this model does not value collateral or recoveries.
investors.formula: Rnet = tickets + sponsors + merchandise + food & beverage − event costs. After priority payments, Pᵢ = αᵢ × residual; Σαᵢ = 1.
investors.gateNotice: Access, eligibility, and any investment require independent checks and transaction-specific documents.

promoters.title: Finance commitments before tickets go on sale.
promoters.lead: Explore capital for artist guarantees and venue holds with explicit risk criteria and ongoing sales visibility.

cards.title: Prepare the transaction
cards.body: Evaluate capacity, demand, price, and costs before committing capital.

cards.title: Connect ticket sales
cards.body: GatePass links tickets, inventory, and access to observable execution.

cards.title: Know the payment order
cards.body: SplitNight lets parties agree the waterfall before the event.

technology.title: Fast operations. Verifiable evidence. Flexible settlement.
technology.lead: Legal wrappers create comfort. Proofs reduce dispute surface.

layers.title: Operating control plane
layers.body: CT-GOT forecasts, diligence, documents, and monitoring remain off-chain.

layers.title: Verifiable proofs
layers.body: RGB-style commitments may link rights and contractual states without publishing sensitive data.

layers.title: Settlement choice
layers.body: Payment rules can use an appropriate rail for each transaction. Cross-domain mechanics are reserved for cases where they add value.

technology.techBody: Client-side validation verifies proofs; data and documents remain in permissioned systems. Signed attestation confirms the closing state. SplitNight's economic split is specified separately from any cross-network exchange mechanism. Use of RGB or digital assets needs specific engineering and legal review.
technology.note: Proposed architecture; each integration needs technical, operational, and legal validation.

market.title: A working-capital opportunity in live touring.
market.lead: The market figures and rates below are company estimates drawn from the PRONESYS material, not audited data or CORTEX historical results.

feeItems.label: carry on profits above preferred return

market.note: Proposed model; actual fees depend on contracts, regulation, and execution.

pilot.title: From event selection to a first measurable transaction.
pilot.lead: Proposed milestones for a 90-day pilot; these are not closed commitments or achieved results.

phases.title: Select and structure
phases.body: Define pilot events, vehicle templates, and evidence sources; score demand.

phases.title: Test financing and ticketing
phases.body: Soft-hold offers, private investor access, GatePass tests, and attested-close workflow.

phases.title: Execute and document
phases.body: Rehearse settlement, finance a first event if conditions clear, and report performance.

pilot.askBody: Strategic capital for an initial cohort, 2–3 financeable opportunities, introductions to promoters and venues, and support for legal structuring.
